## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Lotte Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [5. April 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.114
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.114
- Datum: 5.4.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 5 Scans

pages.transcription:
Newyork, 5.4.41
Dear Hanna & Manfred, I am still troubled by the ~~th~~ thought
that you misunderstood our first letters about Eva and probably
had a bad time thinking that not only was she in unsuitable and
uncongenial surroundings, but also on the other hand criticized
by us. I hope that our later letters-which you have surely re-
ceived in the meantime-have reassured you about both points,
and so that you feel content in the thought that now Eva is in
the right and pleasant surroundings, a kind of old-fashioned
family-life coupled with modern-but not super-modern education
methods and understanding, and that our feelings against her are
just the same as ever, and I believe hers for us too. She has
written us frequently, and is looking forward to be with us soon,
just as we are looking forward to having her. I am sorry we
haven't seen her during our stay in Newhaven as we had intended
to. But as Stefan wrote you, I have not been too well, and
that absorbed much time and energy and occasionally even forced
Stefan to look after me instead of being served and waited on
himself. But he did it nicely and willingly and hardly felt sorry
for himself. Now I am in treatment by Trend's former doctor,
get Calcium-injections, iodine, nose-drops, spend every evening half
an hour in the bathroom with the hot tap on to make it a kind
of steam-or inhalation room. Besides those allergic tests will now be
made and I am looking forward to learn against what strange
objects my poor body reacts so unpleasantly. But you must not
think that I was in a very bad condition and that there is anything
to worry about. Only the last years have spoilt me and I don't
want to put up any more with even moderate asthmatic conditions.
Eva will come next Thursday to stay with us
for a week, and as we have a radio, a kitchenette, an adjoining
room for her and I am not too busy at present, I hope she
will have a pleasant time in New York. I had thought of
inviting at least Robin once, but it seems that he is going
to stay with orthodox friends over passover. At the end of April
I shall go with Eva to visit Elizabeth one Sunday. She has a
girl of 11 and a boy, a year or two older, and I like her to
know at least one of her many cousins. - Yesterday I phoned
to Eva to make arrangements about her coming; I thought that
she might just be going to bed but instead she was just
going out (8 in the evening) to some school festival. The other
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf zwei Seiten (Vorder- und Rückseite). Tinte violett. Die erste Seite ist gut lesbar.
Rückseite des ersten Blattes, zeigt den durchscheinenden Text der Vorderseite (bleed-through). Leer.

pages.transcription:
2) day she wrote she was just busy preparing a cake for auntie
Olga's birthday, another time that she had been to a concert or
that auntie Olga had just read them a story by her husband,
etc, so she is busy and happy, and Mrs. Schatffer[?] whom I am
going to see soon also-told me yesterday on the phone how well Eva
is developping. Well, soon we will have Eva here and shall
write you about everything and also have her photographed for you.
I saw your photos in her room and feel sorry that we haven't got any.
I cannot say that I liked the photos-as photos-so much yet
I would be glad if you could send me some in postcard size.
- We have not been photographed since Brazil and enjoyed the
anonymous life. Now we are again in doubts about our dispositions
from June onward. We do not like to travel again, but there are
a number of reasons for returning to Brazil, at least temporarily,
and we are undecided and not at all sure that we will do it.
In any case we would only think of the Brazilian winter. But
all this is still very vague, and we do not like the idea.
I hope that you are all well and that you spend
a pleasant long weekend at Easter in Bath; it must be spring
there already while here we have still winter although at least
the cold wave is over.
Kindest regards to all and
best love and kisses to you, Lotte
pages.notes: Zweite Seite des Briefes. Handschriftlich, violette Tinte. Gut lesbar.
Rückseite des zweiten Blattes, zeigt den durchscheinenden Text der Vorderseite (bleed-through). Leer.
